solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Head teacher has worst members of school

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of teacher is used

parts.note: to worst someone is to defeat them, as does a rout

explanation.surface: A headmaster who boasts of having the most badly behaved pupils in the school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worst' is a verb here, to beat, not the superlative it pretends to be; 'has' just joins the pieces. School is a school of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish such as these swim together in groups called schools, so the fish are its members.

clue.text: Inspire judge bored by going on vacation

indicators.note: the judge word is pierced by the pair of letters

parts.note: a trier is one who tries a case, a judge

indicators.note: the word is vacated, emptied of its middle, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: A bored judge inspired by going on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vacation' here means emptying out the word going, leaving GG.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off or prompt a reaction is to spark or provoke it.

clue.text: Blue and green

definitions.meaning: risque or smutty, as with a rude joke

explanation.surface: Two colours placed side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes both a smutty joke and feeling a bit unwell.

clue.text: Prime factors in other set are prime

indicators.note: only the letters in prime positions, second, third, fifth, seventh and eleventh, are kept as factors; the rest go

explanation.surface: A number theory claim about the prime factors of another set.
explanation.walkthrough: Number the eleven letters of 'other set are' and keep those at positions 2, 3, 5, 7 and 11.
explanation.definitionFit: The number is divisible only by one and itself, so it is a prime number.

clue.text: Scan radio waves for remote people

indicators.note: the letters of scan radio move about like waves, rearranging into new order

explanation.surface: Scanning the airwaves to reach people living far away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waves' looks like radio waves in the surface but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhabitants of Orkney, islands off the far north of Scotland, are remote from most of Britain.

clue.text: Cockney stocking merchant's branch

indicators.note: Cockneys famously drop their aitches, so the initial H goes

parts.note: a hosier sells stockings and socks

explanation.surface: A London trader in stockings opens a branch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Branch' looks like a shop branch; it is a willow twig. Cockney is the dialect of working-class East London. The 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A willow shoot used in basketry is a pliable twig or branch.

clue.text: Most well-endowed church established binding relationships

indicators.note: the abbreviation wraps round the word for relationships

parts.note: ties are bonds or relationships

explanation.surface: A wealthy church binding people into relationships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well-endowed' looks like a rich church but means busty.
explanation.definitionFit: A superlative of having a large bust, the most buxom.

clue.text: Outlaw speed bumps on windy road

indicators.note: speed is jolted about, its letters rearranged
a winding road twists, so its letters are twisted round

explanation.surface: An outlaw fleeing over speed bumps along a winding road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A reckless bandit of the Wild West is a lawless criminal.

clue.text: Part of cyberattack redirected essential oil

indicators.note: the section is sent the opposite way, read backwards
only a section of the word is taken

explanation.surface: An online attack that rerouted an essential oil supply.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrant perfume oil distilled from rose petals is an essential oil.

clue.text: Unaffected by virtue of religious training

parts.note: since means because of, by virtue of
RE is religious education, a school subject

explanation.surface: Someone unspoiled because of a religious upbringing.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is Religious Education, a British school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Genuine and without pretence, a person is natural and honest.

clue.text: Reason building cover is not creating issue

parts.note: to reason something out is to deduce or infer it
a tile covers a roof, part of a building

explanation.surface: An argument that a building's cover is no problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' means offspring, not a problem; 'is' joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue means children, so something unable to produce offspring is barren.

clue.text: Dye changing appearance of a material

indicators.note: the letters of the dye word are given a new look, rearranged

parts.note: a stain is a dye for wood or cloth

explanation.surface: A dye alters how a piece of fabric looks.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram works on STAIN, the word for 'Dye', swapping its middle letters; 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth glossy fabric woven from silk or similar fibre is a material.

clue.text: Follow great travel programme to understand corruption engulfing Sky

indicators.note: the word for understand swallows the word for sky

parts.note: to get something is to understand it
to lob a ball is to sky it, hit it high
rot means decay or corruption

explanation.surface: A TV viewer told to follow a great travel show to see how corruption has engulfed Sky television.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky looks like the broadcaster but is a verb: to sky or lob a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: To roam the world as a tourist is to follow a grand programme of travel.

clue.text: Eastern European country's volte-face causing uneasiness

indicators.note: a volte-face is an about-turn, so the country's name is read backwards

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland

explanation.surface: An Eastern European country's sudden U-turn makes its neighbours uneasy.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link; turning EIRE about gives ERIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spooky or uncanny gives a feeling of unease.

clue.text: Opportunity university runs in moderate or good number of degrees?

parts.note: room for something is scope or opportunity

indicators.note: the university and runs letters go inside the word for moderate

parts.note: temperate means moderate, not extreme
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Reads like a choice between a university education and a moderate number of degrees.
explanation.walkthrough: Degrees are of temperature, not academic awards; 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The usual comfortable indoor warmth, around twenty degrees Celsius, is a pleasant number of degrees.

clue.text: Couple calmer without daughter in car

parts.note: a couple is two

indicators.note: the daughter letter is dropped out

parts.note: sedater is more sedate, calmer

explanation.surface: A couple more relaxed without their daughter riding in the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-place sports car or roadster seats just a pair of people.

clue.text: Absurd demand during middle of night is aggravating

indicators.note: the word is made absurd, jumbled into nonsense

parts.note: in means during, as in in the night

indicators.note: the central letter of night is taken

explanation.surface: An unreasonable demand in the middle of the night is infuriating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something infuriating is aggravating in the everyday sense of irritating.

clue.text: New university man admits having limited ability to bond

parts.note: uni is the informal short form of university

indicators.note: the servant word lets the letter in

parts.note: a valet is a gentleman's man, his manservant

explanation.surface: A new university man is shy about forming bonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a manservant here; bond is chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry, an atom with a valency of one can form only a single bond.

clue.text: AC current generator?

parts.note: AC looks like alternating current, but it also stands for the cooling system that generates a current of cool air

explanation.surface: An electrical device producing alternating current.
explanation.walkthrough: AC is read as the short form of the cooling system, and the current is a flow of air.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooling system in a building blows a current of chilled air, and AC is its abbreviation.

clue.text: Football manager made up story easy to relate to

indicators.note: in a down light, made up means raised, read from bottom to top

parts.note: the FA, Football Association, governs English football
a fable is a story

explanation.surface: A football manager who tells tall tales is friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made up' looks like 'invented' with story, but turns FA upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A friendly, approachable person is good-natured and easy to talk to.

clue.text: Received third in mathematics degree surprisingly

indicators.note: the letters rearrange unexpectedly
the third letter of mathematics is taken

explanation.surface: A student who surprisingly got a third-class degree in maths.
explanation.walkthrough: A third is the lowest UK honours degree class.
explanation.definitionFit: To welcome a guest is to receive them.

clue.text: Father slept naked and didn't move an inch

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest

indicators.note: stripped of its outer letters, the word for slept loses its covering

parts.note: dozed means slept lightly

explanation.surface: Dad slept with no clothes on and lay motionless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naked' strips DOZED of its first and last letters, leaving OZE.
explanation.definitionFit: To become rigidly still, as with fear, is to stay perfectly motionless.

clue.text: Classic song from middle of Tommy?

indicators.note: the soldier word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: Tommy Atkins is slang for a British private soldier

explanation.surface: A golden hit from the Who rock opera Tommy.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy looks like the rock opera but is a British soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known song from years past is a golden hit, a classic.

clue.text: Ice hotel I'm in at Easter is stifling

indicators.note: the words smother the answer inside them, holding it within

explanation.surface: A guest in an ice hotel at Easter finds it suffocating.
explanation.walkthrough: Ice is slang for kill, the definition, not a frozen hotel; the run spans hotel, I'm, in, at, Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gangster slang to ice someone is to murder them, to wipe them out.

clue.text: State backing popular contribution to debate?

indicators.note: the stating word comes behind the popular word

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
to put something is to state it

explanation.surface: A state backing a popular cause in a debate.
explanation.walkthrough: State is a verb, to express, not a country.
explanation.definitionFit: A contribution or comment one offers in discussion is one's say.

clue.text: Brought up breakfast after losing second part of intestine

indicators.note: in a down light the word is raised, read from bottom up
the cereal word loses a letter

parts.note: muesli is a breakfast cereal

explanation.surface: Vomiting breakfast after a second bout of gut trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought up' suggests vomiting but signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: The final stretch of the small bowel, before the large bowel, is part of the gut.

clue.text: Last items of skincare product on offer behind cleanser

indicators.note: the final letters are placed after the offer word

parts.note: a bid is an offer, as at an auction

indicators.note: the final letters of each of the two words are taken

explanation.surface: The last of a skincare product on sale, with a cleanser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A low basin used for washing one's lower body is a bathroom cleanser of sorts.

clue.text: Device put into operation

definitions.meaning: to carry out or execute a plan

explanation.surface: A gadget being switched on and used.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means a tool; as a verb it means to carry out a plan.

clue.text: Look at correct planting book for flower

indicators.note: the book letter is planted between the other two words

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it
right means correct

explanation.surface: Look at a proper gardening book to identify a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Planting' sounds like gardening, but here it means setting the book letter down between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphrasia is a small wild plant with white blooms, once used to treat eye ailments.

clue.text: Hushed return of opening of Te Deum is gripping

indicators.note: the assembled letters are read backwards
the second word of the hymn's title holds the letter inside it
only the first letter of Te is used

explanation.surface: A choir's hushed rendering of the start of the Te Deum hymn is gripping.
explanation.walkthrough: DEUM gripping T gives DETUM, which turned round gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hushed sounds are quiet and softened, damped down in volume.
